Name: -1_manor_village_maiden_servant
Representative_Docs:
["Oh, we poor manor spirits  
Other poor laborers  
Ordinary third ones  
Helper spirits fourth  
Drinkers fifth  
Were driven to howl at night  
To march across the land  
To walk across the desert.  
Night is painful, moon is painful  
God’s fire is painful  
Night is painful, I cut the hay  
Moon is painful, I cut the stack  
God’s fire is painful,  
Golden rakes in the shed  
Silver sickle handles  
When will I escape the manor's year?  
The manor’s year is a hellish year.  
I escape as if from under your mouth  
Between the jaws of a lion.  
Between the teeth of a monkey  
Now I look back carefully  
On my dog’s load I turn my head.  
Before the home gate  
Before father’s barn door,  
Before brother’s chamber threshold  
Then I look over the ridge  
Towards the worse side,  
See how the hell looks  
The underworlds blaze  
Hell’s windows glow red  
Ghost towers stand idle  
Life seems a joke.  
There are large German fields  
Bottomless lady’s fields.  
There our feathers melt  
Silver ornaments straighten out.  
Wallets grow empty.  
There on the big field  
On the bottomless field.  
On the angular meadow.  
Now I say again in reverse.  
To sing again in Danish  
I turn the words upside down.  
There fall on the back of the German  
Break the mistress’s neck  
Lady’s hip bones fall apart  
Virgin’s limbs twist  
Our backs become whole  
Our scythes sharp  
Our necks stiff.", 'If the maiden dies  
Where then shall I bury the maiden?  
Under the golden church  
Under the slim tower  
Who visits the maiden’s grave there?  
Every month the kings come  
Every Friday the Germans from Riga  
The Germans from Paide ask for prayer  
Let me tell it again,  
Let me sing it back again  
If the boy dies  
Where then shall I bury the boy?  
In the swamp under the big spruce  
Under the broad meadow’s alder  
In the street on the farmstead  
In the gate, in the manure pit  
Who visits the boy’s grave there?  
Every month the devils come  
Every Friday the servants from Riga  
The servants from Paide ask for prayer  
Old boys, loud boys  
Are taken to the mill to sleep  
To make a nest in the threshing barn  
There where the tar road stretches  
The old wheel’s grease trail  
You will stay, you will stay  
Stay feeding the bait  
Look into the water  
Be plump, our maidens  
Be loud, old girls  
The mockers will come  
The maiden’s laugher scorner  
Their mouths big and jaws wide  
Tongues like church doors  
Tines like gate latches  
The dangers driven away  
I understand, answer again  
My dear, little brother,  
If you care for me  
I will care for you  
I care for your paths  
I slander the wide field paths  
I care for the tin belt  
I slander the broad face  
I mock the long dresses  
You have five blisters under your toes  
Six scars on your face  
Seven  
Elbows bent  
Knock your teeth out.', "Now permission is granted to spy
It is nice to go to the sauna
Beautiful to shout with a turnip
Now the reins are held by the old woman
The bridle is in the brother’s sleeve
The reins are held by my own.
When the reins can be held by the fool
The bridle is held by the madman
The bridle is in the man's sleeve,
Then I ask permission from the cap
To the wise one from six
Whether the cap allows me to the village
Thanks to another household
An apron to another room
A clog to the building
The cap does not allow to the village
Thanks not to another household
An apron not to another room
A clog not to the building
I sneak away like a pig to sleep
Go like a lamb to bed
Pull my knees up to my chest
Elbows to my sides
Fists near the heart
Warmth flows from the knees to the belly
Warmth from the elbows to the sides
Warmth from the fists to the heart
I get up in the morning
Elbow water was under the side,
There was a knob of water on top
Jelly water under the heart
Rolling tear water
Eyebrows in a drop of water
When I grow up at home
I sat in father's room
I sat in mother's room
I looked into the brother's room
I grow like hemp in the ditch
I rise like a strawberry in the house
Long pipe in the corner of the room
Neither the old woman has beaten me enough
Nor the old man beaten me enough
To frolic with the mild brother
A straw was the old woman's rod
A cattail was the old man's rooster
A willow leaf was the brother's twig
I got to a bad man
To a wicked companion
Oh, my unruly hair
Or my honeycomb
Dear golden-haired one
I am beaten with a fist
My bottom is pinched
My palm is clipped."]

Name: 0_young maiden_maiden_hay_grandmother
Representative_Docs:
['Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last on the other side  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
I placed gold upon her head  
He mowed the hay in the nook of the forest  
He took the glade in the trap of the forest  
Then her knees began to ail  
Her soft eyes to sleep  
Her shoelaces to untie  
Her apron strings to ache  
I asked the woman  
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last on the other side  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
I placed gold upon her head  
He mowed the hay in the nook of the forest  
He took the glade in the trap of the forest  
Then her knees began to ail  
Her soft eyes to sleep  
Her shoelaces to untie  
Her apron strings to ache.  
The woman heard and answered back  
Young men, like her brothers  
Throw city boys into mud  
Barley was lying straight  
Oats into two middens  
Then make good beer  
Taste the sweet mead  
Make a fine brandy  
Knead bread to be tough  
Then the wife will be healthy  
Healthy and strong  
Then the time came for the child to roll  
Then the son came home  
Prepared for his time.', 'Where must I go  
Where must I lay my head  
It was bad to go to the gray place  
It was nasty to drown in the lake  
Father despised me from the knees down  
Mother despised me from the sleeves up  
Sisters shunned me from the yard  
Brothers from the field with the grain  
The parish from the church path  
Where must I go  
Where must I lay my head  
To give way under my feet  
To wither in the middle of my body  
I will go as a mole into the soil  
As a rat into the grass nest  
I will go as a mole digging mole hills  
As a rat making rat holes  
As a mouse the lady of beauty  
The mole brought me a black hat  
The rat brought a hat made of grass  
The mouse adorned me with jewelry  
Siim dressed me in silk clothes  
Then I go under the village swing  
A ring shines on my finger  
A necklace glimmers round my neck  
All these Germans pondered  
Lords marveled  
Whose beautiful lady is this  
Whose pretty maiden  
I am the bad child of the old woman  
I am the bad child of the old man  
Let the story end, to be told again.', 'I saw the maiden growing;
By the blue fence
Swelling with a red wreath;
Rising in a tin crown.
I, from the stables;
From the coal-black haven,
From the window I gave barley,
In the shadows I carried water;
Without the old woman's knowledge,
Without the old man's knowledge,
That I gained the horse's strength.
In front I put sturdy irons;
Behind irons from the threshing floor.
Then I harnessed the horse.
After that I put on the bridle,
On top I put a playful bow,
Eyes into silk reins,
Eyebrows into golden rings,
Tail into a braid,
Brushed the mane to one side.
I rode to the father-in-law's door,
I rode to the mother-in-law's door:
"Hello, father-in-law! Boot-tops,
Hello, mother-in-law! Neck of the kettle,
Are your maidens at home?"
The mother-in-law understood, answered:
"Our daughters are at the well,
Drawing water at the well."
I ride to the well road:
"Hello, dear maiden!
Drawing water with the bucket,
To water all the village's herd;
To water my horse at the well.
Let my black one paw,
Let my gray one sway,
Let my dappled one tug,
Move on the linen cloth.
I, a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands;
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
A postman from St. Petersburg."
The maiden hears, answers again:
"You are not a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands,
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
Postman from St. Petersburg.
You are an evil suitor,
And a deceitful groom:
Why is your horse harnessed?
Brushed mane and swayed tail?
Why do you have locks on the bridle?
Why do you have an eagle's skull?
A headgear in the harness?
A sparrow in the reins?"
I heard, answered again,
"I have at home an old father
Who makes the locks on the bridle.
I have at home a little brother
Who is my horse's groom,
Brushed mane and swayed tail.
He puts the tail in a braid,
Eyes in silk reins,
Ears in golden rings.
I have at home a little sister
Who makes the letters on gloves
Who makes lace on the whip..."']

Name: 1_swing_wreath_wood_pasture
Representative_Docs:
["Swing smiths, dear brothers  
Look where they have made a swing  
Made a swing below the village  
To the guests' gathering places  
To the village boys' stick fields  
From where the swings were brought  
Swings brought from the Kei village  
Kei village, Pei farmstead  
Fathers brought from long ago  
Moss from the blue pastures  
Straw brought from the meadows  
Swing smiths, dear brothers,  
Little sisters, dear ones  
Silver beads shining  
Let's go to swing on the swings  
The boy comes to swing on the swings  
To sing the swing song  
He comes from afar, rows eagerly  
So that I shine wider than the field  
Shine wider, cover the land  
So that I shine over the forest  
Over three spruce forests  
There were three forests nearby  
One was an apple orchard forest  
That belonged to the young women  
Another a dear birch forest  
That was the young girls'  
The third a precious spruce forest  
That was the young men’s forest.", 'Where has our swing been brought from?  
Where has it been brought from, where has it been obtained?  
Who is bringing our swing,  
Who is bringing it, who is receiving it?  
Toomas is bringing, Sander is receiving.  
The beams were brought from Arjamaa,  
The shaft was brought from Võhmuta,  
The steps from Sinisalu.  
So a new swing was made,  
Will this swing carry us?  
If it does not carry, let it perish.  
Swing smiths, eldest brothers,  
Bring fire, burn the swing,  
Bring water, soak the swing,  
You yourself, hew the swing frame.  
Come, women of the swing village,  
Bring chickens, bring eggs,  
Bring vessels for weaving,  
Bring a pair of ducks;  
The hen stayed at home to lay eggs,  
The rooster stayed at the yard crowing.', "Come to the swing, village girls  
Bring chickens, bring eggs  
Bring geese for hatching  
Bring ducks for brooding  
Ten girls in the village  
Nine across the street  
The tenth, the smith's daughter of the village  
They were allowed to come to the swing  
Afraid the gold would wear out  
The silver beads fade away  
The bright eyes grow pale  
There were many swinging on the swing  
Many swaying on the swing’s beam  
There are no singers on the swing  
No ones singing on the swing plank  
I praise the swing frame  
May the swing-makers be healthy  
Who made the swing to the berry hill  
Among the blue flowers  
In the red alder growing  
Between the beautiful birches  
Kind swing-makers, dear brothers  
Please let it down for me  
If you don’t let it down, I won’t ask  
Then I’ll sway till evening  
Swing till midday  
Surely then the young woman will milk the cow  
Surely then the old man will drive the herd  
If the young woman does not milk the cow  
Nor the old man drives the herd  
Surely then the alder will milk the cow  
Surely then the birch will drive the herd  
The maple tree will give water to the calf  
I hear the village swinging  
Singing on the swing plank  
Waiting for the crowd to call out  
Afraid the crowd will shout  
The crowd does not call me out  
Nor does the crowd shout at me."]

Name: 3_bride_daughters_maiden_wedding
Representative_Docs:
["Among us is a proud girl  
She was a white girl in the parish  
Mareta from Keskküla, the nice one  
She was the village's pride  
Taken out in full bridal attire  
To her mother's wedding.  
Celebrations were held - for the couple  
Then illness began to come  
Hard days started ahead  
Joosep also told Kaie  
Oh, my poor young girl!  
Where should I lay you?!  
You must not be taken before the elders  
You must not be brought before the wise ones  
Not to your father Marjus's house  
Nor to your mother's beloved chamber  
I will send you to the pigsty  
In your clean wedding clothes.  
Joosep asked Kaie,  
Whose own is this?  
Kaie laid her head on the pillow  
Eyes inside the clothes  
Joosep asked a second time  
Oh, my young wife  
Tell your father  
Whose own is this?  
Kaie struck her fist on her chest  
Like a sturdy oak cup  
Nine are your fathers  
The tenth swings Kaie.", "Let's go to the Koiki bride's meadow
Daughters of the Koigi smith
The smith of Koigi had three daughters
One was Anne - the second Kaie
The third slippery Liisukene
Anne was naked by the stove
Kaie was bare-legged by the ironing board
Liisu was under the flax bundle
Anne was meant for me
And Kaie was also bargained for me
I will not take Anne as a wife
Nor do I want to marry Kaie
Anne had torn shirt sleeves
Kaie had broken stockings
I crawled around Liisu
Liisu had beautiful linen.", "Oh our dear brothers or we brothers-in-law  
Together we are stepbrothers  
We eat the same food  
We drink the same drink  
We do not take the same wife  
One takes another wife  
One takes another old woman's daughter  
One takes another old man's daughter  
You take Maie, I take Kaie  
Kaie was quick with work  
Mai was clumsy with her foot  
Anne was assigned to me  
And Kaie was traded to me  
I do not take Anne as a wife  
Nor do I take Kaie as a wife  
Anne was given torn shirts  
Kaie had broken sleeves  
I flirted around Liisu  
Had to go to Pilla  
I ended up sleeping with Malle  
Malle was sweeter to me  
Than those Pilla's milk cakes."]
